summary: Nanofighters is an interactive educational strategy and decision-making game designed to combat misinformation surrounding antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Grounded in real scientific findings from NASA/ISS (Microbiome, 2024), the UN, and global epidemiological studies, the game puts players in command of nanobots defending against bacterial outbreaks. In every round, prevention and treatment choices directly alter bacterial mutation and drug resistance in real time. Nanofighters addresses the challenge by turning complex Earth and space biological trends into hands-on, accessible learning. This is critical because drug-resistant superbugs could kill 39 million people by 2050 on Earth and are already mutating aboard the International Space Station, threatening both terrestrial ecosystems and long-duration space missions.
details: Nanofighters is an interactive educational strategy and decision-making game grounded in real scientific data on antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Across progressive evolutionary stages, players take command of the defense line (nanobots) within a dynamic microscopic environment. In every round, players must make rapid prevention, containment, and treatment decisions in the face of bacterial outbreaks. Its standout mechanic is real-time biological consequence: every choice, whether right or wrong, directly alters the mutation rate, drug resistance, and survival of the bacteria on the board, simulating how the indiscriminate use of antibiotics accelerates the emergence of superbugs. Instead of presenting static charts or theoretical texts on molecular biology, we transformed the very process of natural selection and genetic mutation into a survival game mechanic. We blended the cosmic aesthetics of human space exploration with the microscopic universe of nanobots, showing players that the exact same biological phenomenon threatening lives in hospitals on Earth also challenges humanity aboard the International Space Station.
